title: Residency-aware RBAC templates and periodic review automation
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated regions require that access reviews and RBAC provisioning respect data residency (tenant residency + jurisdiction), and they need automated evidence exports for audits. Current RBAC templates are global and reviewers get noisy signals (lots of unrelated entitlement rows). Scope: implement residency-aware RBAC template layer, surface reviewer-scoped certification runs (per-tenant, per-region), add SCIM reconciliation hooks to tag changes with residency metadata, and wire an evidence exporter for review runs.

Goals:
- RBAC templates support residency constraints and tenant-default residency tags
- Periodic certification runs can be scoped to tenant/residency and delegated to local reviewers
- SCIM hooks persist residency metadata on user/group events (provision/update/deprovision)
- Evidence exporter emits signed, timestamped bundles per review run (CSV + JSON manifest + hash) to S3-like storage for auditors

Proposed design:
1) Template layer: extend role templates with an optional "residency_policy" field (region code list) and evaluation fallback rules. Templates are compiled at assignment time to produce tenant-scoped grants.
2) Reviewer scoping: certification service accepts tenant_id or residency_code filters and computes reviewer worklist by filtering only grants with residency metadata.
3) SCIM reconciliation: add a lightweight event enrichment service that listens to SCIM change events and attaches residency metadata from tenant config; events stored in event store with residency tags and sequence numbers for replay.
4) Evidence exporter: after each certification run produce an evidence bundle (manifest.json, results.csv, signer.sig) uploaded to customer-controlled S3 bucket or platform retention bucket, with a signed hash and audit log link.

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Adding residency tags increases index cardinality in entitlement DB; chosen approach: store residency as a separate indexed column to keep queries efficient.
- Strong consistency vs eventual for SCIM reconciliation: to avoid blocking critical paths, SCIM hook is best-effort with replay; certification run will revalidate entitlements at run-time (double-check against authoritative data).
- RBAC template evaluation cost: compile-on-write (when assignment changes) rather than compile-on-read to reduce runtime overhead.

Acceptance criteria:
- RBAC template API accepts residency_policy and applied grants include residency metadata in DB for 95% of assignments within 5s of creation
- Certification UI/worker can run a tenant-scoped review and present only relevant grants to a delegated reviewer
- SCIM event enrichment service attaches residency metadata for create/update/deprovision events; reconciliation tests cover idempotency and replay
- Evidence exporter produces signed bundles and uploads to configured bucket; automated smoke test verifies manifest and hash

Test plan:
- Unit tests for template compiler, residency-policy evaluation, and SCIM enrichment logic
- End-to-end test: create tenant with residency X, assign template with residency allowed X, run certification and verify review worklist, then run evidence export and verify bundle contents and signature
- Load test: simulate 10k entitlement recomputes across tenants and verify median assignment latency stays <100ms for compile-on-write path

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag the residency_policy field (off by default).
- Opt-in tenants in staging > canary > production.
- Monitor metrics: %assignments with residency tag, certification false-positive rate, evidence export success rate.

Open questions:
- Should we allow multi-region reviewer delegation (one reviewer authorized for multiple residencies)? (P0 discussion item)
- Retention window for exported evidence (default 7 years for enterprise customers?) need legal guidance.
